verification_methodology_note: This track uses a DISTINCT verification tier from this corpus's primary MOJ-portal method (this law is a Council-of-Ministers/Bureau-of-Experts instrument, not a MOJ-issued one, and is absent from the MOJ legal portal), but is MEANINGFULLY STRONGER than the Anti-Bribery Law track's secondary-source-convergence-only tier: the PRIMARY source here is a genuine official government structured database — the Bureau of Experts (هيئة الخبراء بمجلس الوزراء) legal portal at laws.boe.gov.sa, LawDetails GUID 16b97fcb-4833-4f66-8531-a9a700f161b6 — reached via the WebFetch tool using an https://r.jina.ai/<url> reader-proxy prefix (direct sandbox network access to laws.boe.gov.sa is blocked; this proxy routes the fetch through Anthropic's own infrastructure instead). The extraction is COMPLETE and GAPLESS: all 83 articles across all 9 chapters (باب), in order, no missing articles. The SECOND source is WIPO Lex (World Intellectual Property Organization's official national-legislation database), entry SA016, https://wipolex-res.wipo.int/edocs/lexdocs/laws/ar/sa/sa016ar.pdf — a scanned, nationally-stamped (الهيئة الوطنية للوثائق والمحفوظات / National Center for Archives and Records) government-submitted document using a different, older production pipeline than the BOE database, making it a genuinely independent source rather than a mirror. This PDF has no usable extractable text layer (legacy custom Arabic font encoding); it was rendered to page images (29 pages) and OCR'd with tesseract-ara. Cross-verification against this second source was an EXTENSIVE SPOT-CHECK, NOT AN EXHAUSTIVE PER-ARTICLE DIFF: approximately 39 of the 83 articles (~47%), spanning all 9 chapters and every chapter boundary, were individually compared and found to match substantively with no wording or meaning divergence (only trivial OCR noise such as ذ/ز glyph confusion). The full document's STRUCTURE (83 articles, 9 chapters, identical order and headings) was confirmed to match between both sources in its entirety. Each article in this track's data is individually tagged with cross_verified_against_wipo_lex (true for the ~39 spot-checked articles, false for the remainder, which rest on the complete BOE primary-source extraction plus the whole-document structural match only). Two other candidate PDF mirrors (ibtissam.sa, nshr.org.sa) were found in an earlier research pass but determined to be the SAME underlying scan re-hosted twice, not independent sources, and were NOT used for this cross-verification. No amendment history was found or flagged by the BOE source for any article; this track therefore treats all 83 articles as اصلية (original), consistent with what the primary source itself presented as the current, in-force (ساري) text — no separate amendment-tracking endpoint (equivalent to the MOJ portal's get-Section-Changes) was found to exist on the BOE portal for this instrument. Committed WIPO Lex PDF sha256: 98e50be4a0d8a3e6c8ab018402acee72145c3aa9919ea702672c0e51ff7d1926. **POST-MERGE CORRECTION (added after a cross-track conflict was discovered while ingesting the Allegiance Commission Law):** Article 5 was originally ingested as اصلية (unamended) based on the BOE portal's base 'نص النظام' view, which displays the as-originally-promulgated 1412H/1992 text without merging subsequent amendments -- this is consistent with how BOE and WIPO Lex catalog amendments as separate instruments rather than inline-merged text. Two amendments were subsequently confirmed genuine and in force: (1) paragraph (ج) was replaced by Royal Order A/135 (26/9/1427H / 19 Oct 2006), the same order that promulgates the Allegiance Commission Law -- confirmed via nezams.com's amendment-annotated text, marefa.org, and English Wikipedia's 'Allegiance Council' article, all independently agreeing; the BOE base view and this corpus's own ar.wikisource.org cross-check were both confirmed to be unmaintained copies of the original text, not evidence the amendment was reverted. (2) paragraph (ب) had a sentence appended by Royal Order A/256 (26/9/1438H / 21 June 2017), the 'single branch' (فرع واحد) succession-diversification restriction -- verified via primary-source OCR of the actual scanned Royal Order PDF (WIPO Lex document sa102), independently corroborated by a Royal Court transmittal circular on the same document. Article 5 is now tagged معدلة with both the original 1412H text and full amendment history preserved (not deleted), and carries a distinct verification_tier (SECONDARY_SOURCE_PLUS_PRIMARY_OCR_CONFIRMED_AMENDMENT) reflecting this different provenance chain from the other 82 BOE-portal-primary-verified articles. The overall track tier is accordingly now MIXED_TIER_SEE_PER_ARTICLE_VERIFICATION_TIER. No other article in this track is known to be affected by an unflagged amendment, but given this discovery, a full article-by-article amendment-history re-audit of this law against BOE's dedicated amendments view (once BOE access is reliable) is recommended as a follow-up, rather than assumed complete.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: This article was corrected post-merge after a cross-track conflict was discovered (see verification_methodology_note for full detail). The exact original wording of paragraph (ب) before ANY amendment (i.e., its 1412H/1992 text) was confirmed identical to its current pre-2017 form via the University of Minnesota Human Rights Library's independent transcription -- but a full systematic re-audit of all 83 articles against BOE's dedicated amendments view has not been performed, so the possibility of other unflagged amendments elsewhere in this law cannot be fully ruled out.
